native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the century 1800–1700 BCE (18th century BCE): Pottery Decoration rises significantly (+1.45 Z) while Pottery Form declines (−1.87 Z), the only such opposite-direction century across 4100–500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Validate variable mapping (PotteryForm==ZKeform, PotteryDecoration==Zkeverz, CE=−BCE, raw==_inter at anchors). 2) Compute century-over-century Z changes on the raw 100-yr anchors; scan chronologically for first century with dDec>0 & dForm<0 exceeding 1 SD of century changes (and 0.5-Z permissive threshold). 3) Cross-check A: within-century OLS slopes on interpolated yearly series. 4) Cross-check B: phase-free sliding 100-yr window on interpolated series. 5) Report per-century summary table and final natural-language answer with explicit BCE interval and effect sizes. Supporting artifacts: analysis/per_century_summary.csv, analysis/plan_inspection.py, analysis/crosscheck_B_debug.py.
